obligations.title: Risk Management Plan
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall document a risk management plan for the device.
The plan shall be part of the risk management file."
extracted_requirements: Produce a Risk Management Plan before risk management activities begin
Plan must be part of the Risk Management File — not a standalone document
Plan must be maintained and updated throughout the device lifecycle

obligations.title: RM Plan Content
obligations.verbatim:
"The risk management plan shall include at minimum: (a) the scope of the risk
management activities; (b) assignment of responsibilities and authorities;
(c) requirements for review of risk management activities; (d) criteria for
risk acceptability, including the criteria used to decide when further risk
reduction is required; (e) method for evaluating overall residual risk;
(f) verification activities; (g) activities related to collection and review
of production and post-production information."
extracted_requirements: Define the scope — which device, which functions, which lifecycle phases
Assign responsibility and authority for risk management activities (named roles)
Define risk acceptability criteria — severity and probability scales, risk matrix, acceptable thresholds
Specify the method for evaluating overall residual risk (§8)
Identify planned verification activities linking risk controls to their evidence
Describe how post-production information will be collected and fed back into the risk file

obligations.title: Risk Acceptability Criteria
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall define the criteria for risk acceptability, including
the criteria to be used to decide when further risk reduction is required and
whether the residual risk is acceptable."
extracted_requirements: Define severity levels (e.g., catastrophic, critical, marginal, negligible) with descriptions
Define probability levels with qualitative or quantitative definitions
Produce a risk matrix mapping severity × probability to risk levels (acceptable / ALARP / unacceptable)
State the criterion for when benefit-risk analysis is required (§7.4)

obligations.title: Risk Management File
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall maintain a risk management file. For each hazard
identified, the risk management file shall allow traceability to: the hazard,
the hazardous situation(s), the estimated risk(s), the risk control measures,
and the residual risk(s) after implementation of the controls."
extracted_requirements: Maintain a Risk Management File — a collection of records providing full traceability for each hazard
Each hazard must be traceable through: hazardous situation → estimated risk → risk control → residual risk
File must be structured to support audit — an auditor must be able to follow one hazard end-to-end

obligations.title: Intended Use & Misuse
obligations.section: §5.2 — Intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall document the intended use and the reasonably foreseeable
misuse. The manufacturer shall identify the characteristics of the device that
could affect safety, taking into account the intended use and reasonably
foreseeable misuse."
extracted_requirements: Document the intended use including: intended patient population, clinical indication, use environment, user profile
Document reasonably foreseeable misuse scenarios — uses outside the intended use that are predictable
Both intended use and foreseeable misuse must feed the hazard identification process (§5.4)

obligations.title: Safety Characteristics Identification
obligations.section: §5.3 — Identification of characteristics related to safety
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall identify and document qualitative and quantitative
characteristics of the device that could affect its safety, and where
appropriate, define limits for these characteristics."
extracted_requirements: Systematically identify device characteristics that could contribute to hazards (use ISO 14971 Annex C as a checklist)
For each safety-relevant characteristic, define acceptable limits or performance criteria where quantifiable
Document results as a record in the Risk Management File

obligations.title: Hazard Identification
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall identify hazards and hazardous situations. For each
identified hazardous situation, the manufacturer shall estimate the associated
risk using available information or data."
extracted_requirements: Identify all foreseeable hazards (energy, biology, data, software, mechanical, chemical, etc.)
For each hazard, trace the sequence of events to a hazardous situation (hazard → failure mode → hazardous situation → harm)
Consider hazards during all lifecycle phases: normal use, foreseeable misuse, maintenance, storage
Document results in a Preliminary Hazard Analysis or equivalent hazard table in the Risk Management File

obligations.title: Risk Estimation
obligations.verbatim:
"For each identified hazardous situation, the manufacturer shall estimate the
associated risk. The estimation shall consider the probability of occurrence of
harm and the severity of that harm."
extracted_requirements: Estimate risk for each hazardous situation using severity × probability from the risk matrix in the plan
Assign qualitative or quantitative values using the scales defined in the Risk Management Plan
Where probability cannot be estimated, list hazardous situations for risk evaluation without numerical estimation
Document risk estimations in the risk management file (e.g., FMEA table)

obligations.title: Risk Evaluation
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall evaluate each identified risk using the risk acceptability
criteria in the risk management plan. This evaluation determines whether risk
reduction is required."
extracted_requirements: Apply the risk matrix from the plan to each estimated risk — classify as acceptable / ALARP / unacceptable
Document the evaluation decision: accept / reduce further / apply benefit-risk analysis
If reduction is required, proceed to §7 risk control — do not accept an unacceptable risk without justification

obligations.title: Risk Control Options
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall identify risk control measures, using one or more of the
following, in priority order: (a) inherent safety by design; (b) protective
measures in the device itself or manufacturing process; (c) information for
safety."
extracted_requirements: Apply risk controls in priority order: (1) design-level elimination, (2) device protective measure, (3) information/labeling
Document the rationale for selecting the chosen control type — explain why higher-priority options were not applicable when skipped
For software: design-level controls include defensive coding, input validation, output limits, redundancy; labeling-only for a software-induced hazard is rarely sufficient at Class C

obligations.title: Risk Control Verification
obligations.section: §7.2 — Risk control implementation; §7.3 — Residual risk evaluation
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall implement the risk control measures and verify their
implementation. After implementation, the manufacturer shall evaluate the
residual risk."
extracted_requirements: Verify that each risk control measure is implemented as specified (implementation verification record)
Evaluate residual risk after controls — re-estimate severity × probability with controls in place
If residual risk remains unacceptable, apply additional controls or proceed to §7.4 benefit-risk analysis
Link each risk control to its V&V evidence in the Risk Management File

obligations.title: Benefit-Risk Analysis
obligations.verbatim:
"If the residual risk is not acceptable, the manufacturer shall use the criteria
defined in the risk management plan to determine whether the medical benefit
of the intended use outweighs the residual risk."
extracted_requirements: Conduct a benefit-risk analysis for any hazardous situation where residual risk exceeds acceptability criteria after all feasible controls are applied
Document the benefit argument: what clinical benefit does the device provide, and why does it outweigh this specific residual risk
If benefit does not outweigh risk, the device cannot be released — the risk must be made acceptable first

obligations.title: Secondary Hazard Evaluation
obligations.section: §7.5 — Risks from controls; §7.6 — Completeness of risk control
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall evaluate whether the risk control measures introduce
new hazards or hazardous situations. The manufacturer shall verify that all
identified hazardous situations have been considered."
extracted_requirements: After applying each risk control, evaluate whether the control creates new hazards (secondary hazards)
If new hazards are created, apply the full risk process to them
Complete a completeness check: verify that every hazardous situation identified in §5 has a documented risk control outcome

obligations.title: Overall Residual Risk Evaluation
obligations.verbatim:
"After all risk control measures have been implemented, the manufacturer shall
evaluate the overall residual risk of the device using the criteria established
in the risk management plan. If the overall residual risk is not acceptable,
the manufacturer shall gather and review information to determine whether the
medical benefit outweighs the overall residual risk."
extracted_requirements: Conduct an Overall Residual Risk Evaluation (ORRE) after all individual risk controls are verified
ORRE considers the cumulative effect of all residual risks — not just individual hazardous situation risks
Document the ORRE conclusion: overall residual risk acceptable / requires benefit-risk analysis
If overall benefit-risk analysis is required, document it formally (not embedded in the ORRE)

obligations.title: Risk Management Review
obligations.verbatim:
"Before commercial distribution, the manufacturer shall review the risk management
process to ensure: the risk management plan has been implemented; the overall
residual risk is acceptable; appropriate methods are in place to obtain relevant
information in the post-production phase."
extracted_requirements: Conduct a Risk Management Review before product release — this is a pre-release gate
Review must confirm: (1) the plan was followed, (2) ORRE is acceptable, (3) post-production monitoring is in place
Document the review outcome in a Risk Management Report
Risk Management Report must be signed by responsible management and included in the Risk Management File

obligations.title: Post-Production Risk Feedback
obligations.verbatim:
"The manufacturer shall establish a system to collect and review information
generated during production and post-production phases. If previously unrecognized
hazards or risks that are no longer acceptable are identified, the manufacturer
shall feed this information back into the risk management process."
extracted_requirements: Establish a Post-Market Surveillance (PMS) system that collects: complaints, adverse event reports, field feedback, publicly available information about similar devices
Review PMS data on a defined cadence against the risk management file
If new hazards or newly unacceptable risks are identified, formally feed back into the risk management process
For PCCP: post-market data from each change iteration must feed back into risk evaluation before the next change is authorized
